newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks rise, outlook uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks rise, outlook uncertain.

text.p: Croatian stocks led by hoteliers extended their gains on Tuesday, but traders were reluctant to speculate on the length of the current upward trend.
"The interest of the public has boosted share prices, but it is impossible to say whether they would continue to rise, stabilise or fall," a trader with a big brokerage said.
He said demand for Istrian hoteliers and confectioner Kras remained strong while investors are looking for other cheap shares which are most likely to go up in the future.
* Of 10 active issues eight were up, one down and one remained flat.
* Most actively traded Zagrebacka banka earned 30 kuna to close at 1,000 on volume of 10,446 shares.
* Istrian hoteliers posted significant new gains:
- Laguna Porec rose 100 kuna to 1,100 on 469 shares traded.
- Riviera jumed 75 kuna to 280 on volume of 322.
- Istraturist gained 45 kuna to close at 230, with 125 shares changing hands.
- Arena went up 40 kuna to 250, with 677 shares sold.
* The interest for hoteliers spread to non-Istrian ones and Suncani Hvar closed at 56 kuna, gaining 6 on a relatively big volume of 4,496 shares.
* Confectioner Kras closed 20 kuna higher at a new high of 680 kuna after peaking at 719 on volume of 1,377 shares.
* The only loser was Podravka food concern, edging one kuna down to 277 on a big volume of 2,364 shares.
* Electric cables producer Elka rose 30 kuna to 220, on 105-share volume.
* Daily share volume was up at 22,302, total turnover higher at 13.8 million kuna.
